description:
The pipeline of a custom OpenSearch analyzer: char filters that clean the raw text, a tokenizer that splits it into tokens, and a chain of token filters that transform those tokens. Direct parallel to an OpenSearch custom analyzer; refer to that page for what each piece does and to the inventories of available char filters, tokenizers, and token filters for the exhaustive list of names and parameters.

Minimal example (standard tokenizer with lowercase folding):

{
  "tokenizer": { "name": "standard" },
  "indexFilterOrder":  ["lowercase"],
  "searchFilterOrder": ["lowercase"]
}

Stemming example (English stop words + Porter stem) — note lowercase comes before stop and stemmer so the English stop list and stemmer see lowercase input:

{
  "tokenizer": { "name": "standard" },
  "tokenFilters": [
    { "name": "english_stop",    "definition": "{\"type\":\"stop\",\"stopwords\":\"_english_\"}" },
    { "name": "english_stemmer", "definition": "{\"type\":\"stemmer\",\"language\":\"english\"}" }
  ],
  "indexFilterOrder":  ["lowercase", "english_stop", "english_stemmer"],
  "searchFilterOrder": ["lowercase", "english_stop", "english_stemmer"]
}

Autocomplete example (edge n-gram at index, plain match at search) — the asymmetric pattern:

{
  "tokenizer": { "name": "standard" },
  "tokenFilters": [
    { "name": "autocomplete_ngram", "definition": "{\"type\":\"edge_ngram\",\"min_gram\":2,\"max_gram\":20}" }
  ],
  "indexFilterOrder":  ["lowercase", "autocomplete_ngram"],
  "searchFilterOrder": ["lowercase"]
}

Synonym example — declare WHERE synonyms go in the chain using the reserved synapse_synonyms token; the SynonymSets listed on the SearchConfiguration are then expanded in place:

{
  "tokenizer": { "name": "standard" },
  "indexFilterOrder":  ["lowercase", "synapse_synonyms"],
  "searchFilterOrder": ["lowercase", "synapse_synonyms"]
}

tokenizer.description: Required. The tokenizer that splits text into terms. Reference a built-in by name (e.g. 'standard', 'keyword', 'whitespace', 'icu_tokenizer') or supply a custom OpenSearch tokenizer definition. See AnalyzerComponent.

charFilters.description: Char filters owned by this analyzer — applied to the raw text BEFORE tokenization. Each entry is either a built-in (e.g. 'html_strip') or a custom OpenSearch char filter. Referenced by name in 'charFilterOrder'.

tokenFilters.description: Token filters owned by this analyzer — applied AFTER tokenization. Each entry is either a built-in (e.g. 'lowercase', 'stop', 'porter_stem') or a custom OpenSearch token filter. Referenced by name in 'indexFilterOrder' and 'searchFilterOrder'.

indexFilterOrder.description:
Ordered token-filter chain applied at INDEX time. Each name is resolved as one of:

  • A filter defined in this analyzer's tokenFilters (rendered with its definition).
  • The reserved token synapse_synonyms (see below).
  • Anything else — passed verbatim to OpenSearch. Works for any built-in like lowercase or for plugin filters like phonetic that ship with AOSS.

Synonym injection: the token synapse_synonyms is the only way to wire SynonymSets into an analyzer. At index-build time it is replaced in place by the qnames listed in the SearchConfiguration's synonymSets, in order; if synonymSets is empty the placeholder is dropped. An analyzer with no synapse_synonyms in its chain will NOT have any synonyms applied even if the SearchConfiguration lists them — by design, so chain authors stay in control of position.

Ordering pitfalls:

  1. Graph-aware filters (synonym_graph, word_delimiter_graph) emit multi-position tokens — a non-graph filter following them can yield an invalid token graph.
  2. word_delimiter_graph BEFORE synonym_graph is rejected by OpenSearch (synonym rules are parsed using preceding filters).
  3. Synonym matching is case-sensitive unless lowercase precedes synapse_synonyms and the rule terms are lowercase.
  4. Conventional stemmer position is AFTER lowercase and AFTER stopword removal — see the OpenSearch stemming guide.

searchFilterOrder.description: Ordered token-filter chain applied at SEARCH time. Optional — if absent the search chain mirrors 'indexFilterOrder' (symmetric analysis, the common case). Set this when the two paths legitimately differ; for example, an edge n-gram autocomplete chain at index time + a plain analyzer at search time. Same name-resolution (owned filter, 'synapse_synonyms' placeholder, or verbatim built-in) and same ordering pitfalls as 'indexFilterOrder'.

charFilterOrder.description: Ordered char-filter chain applied to raw text before tokenization. Used for both index-time and search-time. Each name is either a built-in (e.g. 'html_strip', 'icu_normalizer') or a filter defined in this analyzer's 'charFilters'.

positionIncrementGap.description: Optional. Sets OpenSearch's position_increment_gap on the analyzer — the position gap inserted between values of a multi-valued field so phrase queries don't match across value boundaries. Defaults to the OpenSearch default (100 for text) when omitted.
